sections.h2: What should a Northbrook homeowner know before selling?
sections.html:
Northbrook is one of the simpler Cook County villages to sell in on paper, because it charges no municipal transfer tax and issues no transfer stamps. The one local step is closing out the water account with a final meter reading.

The village sits on the North Shore in Cook County, spreads over about 13 square miles, and borders Lake County to the north. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 34,744 residents. Housing is mostly owner-occupied and high in value, so the local process is short and most of a seller's effort goes into pricing and condition.

This page covers the Northbrook rules, the Cook County steps that apply, and how a direct sale compares with a listing.

sections.h2: What is Northbrook like for sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
Northbrook began as Shermerville, named for the man who gave land for its first railroad station, and took its present name in 1923. It was incorporated in 1901. The population climbed from 3,319 in 1950 to 30,735 by 1980, and the last working farm closed in 1987. The village was also the first community without a Lake Michigan shoreline to filter lake water for public use.

  • Several elementary districts, numbered 27, 28, 30 and 31, serve the village, and High School District 225 feeds Glenbrook North High School. A small northwest corner falls in Wheeling's District 21, and a southeast sliver is in Sunset Ridge District 29.
  • Metra's Milwaukee District North Line stops at Northbrook station on Shermer Road downtown.
  • Shopping runs along Sanders Road, Skokie Boulevard and Lake Cook Road, and Northbrook Court opened in 1976.
  • Allstate is the largest employer, and Astellas and Barilla have North American headquarters in the village.
  • The Northbrook Park District runs Techny Prairie Park and Fields, a 113-acre park along the West Fork of the North Branch of the Chicago River.

Because the school district boundaries cross house by house, a listing should name the exact elementary and junior high district for the address. The village's Know Your Neighborhood tool shows zoning and school districts by property.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Northbrook housing?
sections.html:
The owner-occupied rate is 87.2% for 2020 to 2024, which makes Northbrook a house-owner village. The table below shows the figures most useful for a pricing conversation.

A 91.9% same-house rate means few homes change hands in a given year, so comparable sales can be thin on a specific block. Ask an appraiser or agent for nearby sales, since the village median hides block-by-block differences.

sections.h2: Does Northbrook charge a transfer tax or require transfer stamps?
sections.html:
No. The village states on its real estate agent page that it does not levy a real estate transfer tax or issue transfer stamps. The Cook County Clerk's municipal transfer tax list, updated October 2025, has no entry for Northbrook either.

The state and county taxes still apply. The Clerk lists the State of Illinois rate as 50 cents per $500 and the Cook County rate as 25 cents per $500, with the seller as the liable party. The state rate comes from 35 ILCS 200/31-10. A sale also needs the PTAX-203 transfer declaration.

sections.h2: What does the village require for the water account?
sections.html:
Northbrook Municipal Code Section 27-63 requires everyone in a property transaction to confirm with the village that a final meter reading was taken and that no unpaid water balance remains. Call the water billing office at 847-664-4171 to set that up.

  • Water is billed quarterly, and sewer and stormwater charges ride on the same bill.
  • If the seller leaves a balance, the code ties it to the property, and it moves to the new owner's account after thirty days.
  • Sellers should close any utility accounts and schedule final reads as part of the sale, per the village's guidance to agents.

Settling the final bill at the closing table avoids a dispute with the buyer later. For liens and other debts, the village points to the Cook County Property Tax Portal and suggests a FOIA request for building permits and other outstanding items on a parcel.

sections.h2: How does Cook County assessment affect a Northbrook seller?
sections.html:
Most of Northbrook lies in Northfield Township, and a northwest corner lies in Wheeling Township. The Cook County Assessor lists both among the north suburb townships on a triennial cycle with reassessments in 2022 and 2025.

Look up your parcel's township and 14-digit PIN on the Assessor's site. The township assessor for Northfield can answer questions about an appeal. For tax installment dates and the balance on a parcel, ask the Cook County Treasurer, because the sale closing statement usually prorates the bill.

sections.h2: How do jobs and commuting shape demand in Northbrook?
sections.html:
The village counts more than 3,000 businesses providing over 45,000 jobs, more than its resident population, based on a 2018 Census Bureau estimate that Wikipedia cites. About 13% of working residents hold jobs inside the village, and roughly 87% commute elsewhere. The Census Bureau puts mean travel time to work at 26.8 minutes for 2020 to 2024.

Allstate, whose campus sits in an unincorporated part of Northbrook, is the largest employer, with about 8,000 workers. Health care, professional services, retail and manufacturing fill most of the rest. For a seller, the practical point is access: Milwaukee District North Line trains, Lake Cook Road, Sanders Road and Skokie Boulevard all matter to buyers who commute, so name them in a listing or offer discussion.

sections.h2: What happens when the deed is recorded in Cook County?
sections.html:
Northbrook deeds are recorded through the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050, which also lists the state and county stamp amounts. The Clerk's list shows the seller as the party liable for the state and county tax, with a rubber stamp as proof of payment.

Because Northbrook has no municipal stamp, the closing package is lighter than in many neighboring suburbs. A seller still needs a signed deed, the PTAX-203 declaration, a clear title, and a final water read. If a trust or estate holds the title, the title company will tell you which exemption language applies.

sections.h2: How do I choose between listing and a direct sale in Northbrook?
sections.html:
With a median value above $650,000, most Northbrook houses sell through a standard listing, since buyers at that price usually arrive with a mortgage. A direct sale makes sense when the house needs more work than a listing can absorb or a family needs a quick, quiet close.

  • Choose a listing when the house is updated and you can wait for showings.
  • Choose a direct cash sale when the property is dated, a tenant or estate issue slows a listing, or you need a firm closing date.
  • Either way, arrange the final water read, confirm liens through the Cook County portal, and order the PTAX-203.

faqs.q: Does Northbrook have a real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The village says it does not levy a transfer tax or issue transfer stamps. State and Cook County transfer taxes still apply on the deed.

faqs.q: What must I do about the water bill when I sell?
faqs.a: Call 847-664-4171 to schedule a final meter reading and pay the balance. Section 27-63 of the municipal code requires the final read, and any unpaid amount moves to the new owner after thirty days.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Northbrook houses?
faqs.a: Elementary districts 27, 28, 30 and 31 serve most of the village, and District 225's Glenbrook North High School serves most of it. Small areas fall in Wheeling's District 21 or Sunset Ridge District 29, so check the exact address.

faqs.q: Which township assessor handles my Northbrook property?
faqs.a: Most of the village is in Northfield Township and a corner is in Wheeling Township. Look up your PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to confirm the township.

faqs.q: How do I check for liens before listing?
faqs.a: Use Cook County's Property Tax Portal to search for liens or debts on the parcel. The village notes the county's records may not be complete, so it suggests a FOIA request for other debts and building permits.
